transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-05-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Cerulean Head of Platform), Sana (Cerulean Infra), Diego (Cerulean Partnerships)
---
Summary: Introductory partner discovery for building a SaaS connector that would let Cerulean resell Redwood-hosted and dedicated inference to their architecture customers. Discussion covered integration patterns (router vs direct egress), auth and SSO, pilot scope, rough commercial model, and initial technical risks (on-prem, VPC peering, KV cache compatibility, quantization artifact differences).
Topics: 1) Partner integration patterns 2) Security/compliance & SSO 3) Pilot success criteria and benchmarks 4) Technical unknowns and next steps
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh it's Maya from Redwood, happy to kick off. We only have about an hour but we want to cover integration patterns and where a pilot could land.
[00:18] Alex: Awesome, thanks Maya. Diego and I are here from the partnerships side, Sana's gonna get into infra details. We want to understand how Redwood would surface in Cerulean's platform — whether we embed calls or proxy through our control plane.
[00:30] Omar: Cool, hi all. Quick intro: I'm Omar, I work on the runtime and routing. We typically see two patterns — a direct API integration where your control plane calls Redwood's hosted API, or using our dedicated / private connectors deployed into your VPC. Both have trade offs for latency and data residency.
[00:48] Sana: Clarify — when you say dedicated, do you mean Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity or something that runs in our VPC?
[00:55] Priya: Good question. Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra but we also have Redwood Private which can be deployed into a customer VPC or on-prem. For partners like you, we can do a hybrid: control plane in Redwood hosted, with inference nodes in the partner VPC, so calls stay inside your network.
[01:12] Diego: We need strong points on the security side — customers ask about SSO, audit logs, and KMS for keys. How does that look?
[01:20] Maya: We have SAML SSO for console/portal and API keys for programmatic. For Private deployments we support KMS integrations and bring-your-own-keys options. We also provide audit logs and token-level usage traces in the console.
[01:34] Alex: Any gotchas around audit log retention for EU customers?
[01:38] Omar: Retention windows are configurable in Private, hosted has default retention but we can offer extended retention as an enterprise add-on. We'll share the security pack and data residency docs.
[01:50] Sana: On the technical side, we run a multi-tenant control plane and would prefer a connector model that avoids double-egress costs. Ideally, our control plane would proxy requests but keep tokens scoped so we don't store user PII. Is prefix/KV cache preserved in that model?
[02:10] Priya: If you proxy through your control plane to hosted Redwood, KV cache benefits are limited because the cache is per-account in our serving runtime. For best token-cost and latency, deploying inference nodes in your VPC (Private) lets you share a local KV cache for repeated contexts. There's middle ground: per-tenant cache in a layer near your proxy, but it's more engineering on your side.
[02:35] Alex: So for an initial pilot — probably proxying to hosted is simplest. Then for larger customers we can onboard dedicated or private. What would a pilot bench look like?
[02:45] Omar: We typically run two benchmarks: latency p95 under expected token lengths and throughput for a synthetic prompt mix. We'll provide a small script that runs against a model variant. If you're concerned about model fidelity, we can run an eval with your prompt set.
[03:02] Sana: Do you provide quantized model variants? Some of our edge customers want cheaper inference and we need to understand quality tradeoffs.
[03:08] Priya: Yes, we curate quantization profiles. We'll call out expected quality deltas per task; for many completion/chat workloads 4-bit quantization is acceptable but some reranking/semantic tasks may see regressions. We'll include recommended quant profiles for typical templates.
[03:24] Diego: Who usually owns the billing flow in a reseller scenario? Cerulean wants to plate on our bill then settle with Redwood, or is it possible for customers to be billed directly?
[03:33] Maya: We support both. Many partners prefer a reseller model where usage is billed to the partner and we provide an invoice to them. We can also do direct billing per customer with consolidated invoicing options. We'll share commercial options in the follow-up.
[03:48] Alex: Can you outline the timeline you typically see for a pilot to production?
[03:53] Omar: For proxy-hosted pilot with canned prompts, 2–4 weeks including integration and smoke benchmarks. For a dedicated or private deployment deeper in your network expect 6–8 weeks for capacity provisioning, networking, and security review.
[04:06] Sana: On networking — VPC peering vs private link — what's recommended?
[04:10] Priya: For low-latency intra-cloud we'd recommend private link style connections. For customers that require on-prem, we support VPN or direct connect. We'll need network diagrams to size egress rules and open ports.
[04:22] Alex: We have a concern — CloudGiant has been pushing similar reseller deals and they promise "zero-configuration" integration. How do you differentiate?
[04:29] Maya: Two ways: runtime performance and observability. Our serving runtime focuses on production economics — continuous batching, KV cache, and model selection for latency/cost tradeoffs. Also the Console gives token-level breakdowns so your customers see unit economics. We can also co-brand the experience.
[04:47] Omar: To add — our routing and fallback policies are tuned for graceful degradation; we can route to lower-cost variants if capacity hits. That tends to beat simple proxy offerings that have brittle fallback.
[04:59] Sana: Any obstacles we should expect around certs / HSM / KMS integrations?
[05:04] Priya: For KMS we integrate with major cloud KMS providers and can support HSM on Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption. We'll include a matrix of supported KMS providers in the security pack.
[05:17] [05:17] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:20] Alex: Ok let's talk about pilot success criteria — what's granular enough for us and the buyer to evaluate value?
[05:28] Maya: Typical success metrics: p95 latency under X ms for typical prompt length, throughput for N sessions per minute, cost per 1k tokens below a threshold you agree with, and a quality check — automated evals with your prompt set showing <= 5% regression vs baseline model.
[05:48] Diego: Quality checks — baseline meaning what? Their current open-source model or CloudGiant?
[05:54] Omar: Baseline typically whatever your customers are using today. In the pilot we can run side-by-side comparisons: your baseline vs Redwood model variant, and produce a small eval report.
[06:05] Sana: For on-prem customers we need a plan to do local inference — do you support an air-gapped option?
[06:11] Priya: We do; Private on-prem packages can be shipped with offline installers. Those require SRE engagement from both sides and longer lead times, but we've done it for regulated industries.
[06:22] Alex: From a go-to-market perspective, Diego wants to understand co-selling / referral compensation.
[06:28] Maya: We'll route you to partnerships for legal and commercial, but high-level: reseller discounts for committed volume, referral credits for early customers, and joint GTM support. We'll loop in our partnerships lead post-call.
[06:40] [06:40] Speaker 2: (overlap)
[06:44] Sana: Ok technical deep dive: Omar, can you sketch how batching interacts with our proxy? If requests come through Cerulean's control plane will you still batch effectively?
[06:53] Omar: Batching is driven on the serving runtime. If proxying to hosted with a single API-key shared across many customers you'll still get batching benefits because requests queue into our runtime. Caveat: if you do one request per tenant to maintain strict isolation, batching efficiency drops. For dedicated/private deployed near you we can provide pooled GPUs and preserve batching across tenants if you choose that model.
[07:18] Alex: Can we get sample numbers? p95 latency change if we go from hosted proxy to private vpc deployment?
[07:25] Omar: Ballpark: hosted proxy p95 might be 250–400ms depending on region and prompt size; private in-vpc could drop to 80–150ms typical. But those numbers vary with model size, sequence length, and whether you turn on continuous batching. We'll run a benchmark.
[07:41] Diego: For the pilot we want to include a stress test that simulates 1k concurrent sessions. Can Redwood produce a simulated load harness?
[07:49] Priya: Yes we'll provide a load harness and scripts — the SE team will help run it with you during the workshop.
[07:56] Alex: Network egress costs are a concern for our customers. If proxying to Redwood hosted, double egress happens — how do you typically minimize that?
[08:05] Maya: Two levers: 1) compress payloads and only transmit deltas where possible, 2) push more inference to dedicated/private nodes to keep traffic local. We'll model egress in the pilot cost spreadsheet.
[08:18] Sana: Does Redwood expose internal metrics over Prometheus or do we only get Console dashboards?
[08:23] Omar: For Private deployments you can pull Prometheus metrics and we can add exporters. Hosted gives you Console dashboards and traces; we can also send metrics to your monitoring via secure push.
[08:36] [08:36] Speaker 3: hmm
[08:38] Diego: Let's lock the pilot scope so we can commit resources. Proposed: 2-week proxy-hosted integration using a set of 20 customer prompts, 1 smoke benchmark, and an eval report. If that looks good we'll schedule a private deployment proof for a single enterprise customer. Thoughts?
[08:54] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll need access to your prompt set and current baseline model details. Omar will own the benchmark and the SE team will run an integration workshop.
[09:04] Sana: I can share the topology and auth flow — we use SAML+OIDC for customers and have an API gateway that terminates TLS.
[09:12] Priya: Great, that's workable. We'll send a checklist for required network rules and sample cURLs for your devs to test.
[09:20] Alex: Any specific telemetry we should include in the pilot to validate UX?
[09:24] Maya: Token-level cost per session, per-route latency, and top-N prompt fallbacks. Also we'll capture false positives for generation safety checks if relevant to your customers.
[09:36] Diego: Ok, risks: 1) model quality drift for quantized variants 2) egress costs 3) legal around data retention — how fast can we get security and legal docs?
[09:46] Maya: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 artifacts in the next two business days; legal templates usually take a week to start redlines, but partnerships will help accelerate.
[09:55] Sana: For the network checklist — can you list ports and IP ranges we need to open?
[09:59] Omar: Yes, we'll provide exact CIDR ranges and recommended ports. For Private we'll do peering, so rules are minimal.
[10:06] [10:06] Speaker 1: (laughs)
[10:10] Alex: Before we wrap — can we summarize agreed deliverables and owners?
[10:14] Maya: Sure. Deliverables: 1) Integration diagram + API spec (Maya, due 2025-05-16) 2) Security pack (Maya/PubSec, due 2025-05-15) 3) Pilot benchmark script and load harness (Omar, due 2025-05-16) 4) Cerulean infra topology and auth flow (Sana, due 2025-05-15) 5) Workshop schedule (Maya to propose a few slots for week of 2025-05-19)
[10:38] Diego: Sounds good. We'll also prepare a one-pager for our GTM team to understand commercial options.
[10:44] Priya: We'll add a short runbook for fallbacks and outage handling during pilot.
[10:49] Alex: Quick question — in the roadmap, you support model rollouts/A-B tests. Would that be available to our customers?
[10:56] Omar: Yes, rollouts and canary deploys are part of Redwood Console; you can configure per-tenant model pins and automatic fallback policies. That helps with safe rollouts across multiple customers.
[11:09] Sana: Final note — storage of prompts and PII. We need clarity on what is stored in logs and how long.
[11:16] Maya: We'll document default retention and encryption; for pilot we can opt-in to minimized retention and pseudonymize data. We'll capture that in the security pack.
[11:27] Diego: Great. Anything else?
[11:30] Alex: No, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the docs.
[11:33] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the diagram and propose workshop times.
[11:37] [11:37] Call ends
